newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei slides in blue-chip sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei slides in blue-chip sell-off.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's benchmark Nikkei average lost almost 1 1/2 percent on Thursday as investors sold blue-chip issues to cash in recent rises.
The selling helped push the Nikkei 225 down 309.74 points or 1.45 percent to 21,035.54 by the close, its largest drop in more than a month.

"On top of profit-taking in global issues, construction company shares crumpled and smaller issues including over-the-counter shares weakened, weighing down the market as a whole," said a broker at a second-tier brokerage.
Turnover fell to 316 million shares from 398 million on Wednesday.
Foreign investors, who had been fuelling the recent market rise, were net sellers on Thursday.

"The Thanksgiving Day holiday in New York on Thursday seems to be subduing foreign investor buying," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities' general manager. "Unless they come back and resume buying, the market will be limp because domestic investors are still very cautious."
Honda Motor Co, the bourse's most heavily traded issue, lost 110 yen to 3,360 yen on turnover of about 7.65 million shares.
Share price fluctuations in Honda reflect those of the market as a whole, in which direction has been provided mainly by foreign investors, brokers said.

"When Honda climbs to new heights, it pulls the Nikkei average with it, masking the issues which are plunging to lows," said Keiji Arai, a strategist at Sanyo Securities. "When Honda falls, everything suddenly becomes very weak."
Among other big losers in blue chips, Canon Inc shed 20 yen to end at 2,470 yen, Toyota Motor lost 20 yen to 3,120 yen, and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries lost 17 yen to 935 yen.
Construction firms were battered by dwindling hopes for more government public spending and worries over the construction industry's financial health.

Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc cut its ratings of some general contractors such as Obayashi Corp which shed 28 yen to 865, Taisei Corp which fell 29 yen to 642 and Shimizu Corp which ended one yen lower at 964.
"As far as portfolios are concerned, we cannot cut out construction firms completely, so a reshuffling of shares is being carried out," an investment trust fund manager said.
